CONTRAST SCOPE IS `body`. ModalRoot PORTALS to the overlay root, so
`[data-probe]` contains none of this dialog and a probe-scoped sweep
reports 0 failures from an empty subtree — the silence measure.mjs now
exits 3 on. The wait names the LIBRARY tab's toolbar rather than the modal
frame, because all four tabs render inside the same frame.
BOARD WON: 1164:4716 puts the 'for <element>' subtitle at 11 where it
shipped 12, and 1746:8390/8392/8394 make the Grid/List pair two 28-high
chips on a 4 radius at 12px — accent-filled for the active one, white on a
--color/border-medium edge for the other. They shipped at flowbite's own
height and its rounded-lg, because `size="xs"` constrains neither: a
default that nothing contradicts is not overridden, it is simply kept.
THE MODAL FRAME AND ITS HEAD ARE NOT JOINED, on the shared-primitive rule.
1164:4713 gives the frame a 16/14 inset and a 12 gap; in the product those
live on MODAL_HEAD_CLASS / MODAL_BODY_CLASS rather than the frame, and
Modal.tsx's own comment records that the 16/14 was MEASURED on this board
184:24). One frame does not re-settle a control six frames agree on, and
the frame's own padding is 0 by construction. Same for the tab PILLS:
1173:4805-4812 draw them 11px on a 5 vertical pad, and chrome-ui Tabs is
measured against 1172:4867 and 1172:4825 as well — its docstring names all
three. The tab ROW (1173:4804) is joined, because gap and fill are this
frame's own arithmetic and agree.
NOT JOINED — THE RESULT GRID, and it is a structural difference rather
than drift. 1164:4721-4730 draw eight bare 140x96 thumbs on a 10 gutter.
The product's AssetCard is a bordered card: thumb, then the file NAME and
SIZE under it. Joining the board's node would compare a 96-tall thumb
against a card that is 96 plus two lines of metadata — and the metadata is
information the board omits, not chrome the product invented. A picker
that shows eight identical grey rectangles and no filenames is not a
target worth conforming to. diff.mjs cannot see structure anyway (README
§What this harness cannot see); this is recorded so the next reader knows
it was looked at.
ALSO NOT JOINED: 1164:4719/4720, the search field — chrome-ui TextInput,
boards.json authority=open:input-fill. 1173:4814, the accepts/limit
footnote — a text frame at w-434 inside a 608 column, which is the frame's
own wrap point rather than a width the product should hold; its copy IS
conformed and carries the board's own limits.
1746:8392 / 1746:8394 (the Grid and List chips themselves) ARE conformed —
accent fill, --color/border-medium edge, 28 high, 4 radius, 12px — but not
JOINED, because each node's only remaining property is a text-hug width (45
and 41) and the browser measures the same labels at 43.84 and 41.95. A
1.16px disagreement between Figma's advance width for 'Grid' at 12px Inter
and Chrome's is export noise, not design, and holding it would need a
literal `w-[45px]` — which Gate 14's layout-literal ratchet bans. The pair's
box IS measured, through 1746:8390 (28 x 90 = 45 + 41 + a 4 gap).
A HARNESS DEFECT WAS FOUND HERE, and it was manufacturing failures rather
than hiding them. The contrast sweep's `parse()` read only `rgb()`/`rgba()`;
Tailwind v4 emits `oklab(0 0 0 / 0.6)` for every `bg-*/NN` opacity modifier.
An unreadable colour returned null, `effectiveBg` treats null as no fill and
composites past it, so AssetCard's eight white-on-black-scrim delete buttons
measured white-on-WHITE at 1.00:1 — eight fabricated WCAG failures on a
control that is perfectly legible. The same silence would hide a REAL
failure on any element whose fill is an oklab/oklch/color() value, which is
every `/NN` opacity in this codebase. measure.mjs now rasterises what the
regex cannot read through a 1x1 canvas, in the browser's own colour engine.
